paragraphs: Securly sells student safety software to K-12 schools and districts, bringing content filtering and wellness visibility into a single platform. The company describes itself as parents, former educators, and technologists working on school safety.

Its content filter is described as the first cloud-native filter built specifically for K-12. A safety monitoring product analyzes online activity for signs of cyberbullying, self-harm, and violence. A classroom tool lets teachers share screens, lock devices, and push resources during a lesson. A digital hall pass product now folds in tardy management, visitor management, and PBIS. A newer layer puts guardrails on student AI use in the same way the web is filtered.

Published case studies name districts such as Ysleta ISD, which the company says uses its AI transparency tools across 34,000 students. For evidence of how widely it is used, Securly cites the EdTech Top 40 report from LearnPlatform by Instructure. Its board includes a managing director from Golden Gate Capital.
